sections.html:
Tuscaloosa County's seat is the city of Tuscaloosa, which stands on the Black Warrior River roughly 60 miles southwest of Birmingham. With 99,600 people in the 2020 census, a 10.1 percent gain on 2010, it ranks fifth among Alabama cities, and the 2025 estimate tops 114,000. Hale and Pickens counties are part of the same metro area, so buyers arrive from a wide region.

The University of Alabama employs more people than anyone else here, and Mercedes-Benz U.S. International leads the industrial list with more than 6,100 workers. The median age of 27.1 shows how many students live in town, and that colors the rental market around campus.

Tuscaloosa spreads over 72.22 square miles, of which 62.15 are land, and Lake Tuscaloosa lies wholly inside the limits. Forested hills rise in the northeast while a low, marshy plain fills the southwest, so soil and drainage change noticeably from one side of the city to the other.

Buyers shop by area: downtown and midtown, the campus district, Alberta and Hillcrest, East and West Tuscaloosa, and North River along the lake and river corridor. Someone selling in Alberta meets different buyers than someone beside the campus. Know where your street falls before you discuss price.

The town was incorporated in 1819, was the state capital from 1826 to 1846, and welcomed the University of Alabama in 1831. That long timeline produced mixed housing. A house near downtown can have dated plumbing, old wiring or a roof patched more than once, and those items often decide whether a financed buyer's inspection goes smoothly or falls apart.

If you own a rental near campus, look at the lease end date before you ask for offers. A house vacated when the lease ends is simpler to show and to transfer. A lease still running may have to be honored by the next owner. Pull together the lease, the rent record and any repair requests so a buyer sees everything at once.

Turnover between students leaves wear: scuffed floors, stained carpet, tired paint. Decide whether you want to repair that yourself or sell as is, and price the choice honestly against what a listing would net.

Violent tornadoes are part of Tuscaloosa's record. An F4 tornado in the county in December 2000 killed eleven people. The EF4 tornado of April 27, 2011, about 1.5 miles wide with estimated 190 mph winds, killed 44 in the city and caused an estimated $2.45 billion in damage.

Every storm conversation in town starts from that day. Buyers and insurers ask about roof age, hail claims and repairs after storms. If hail or wind hurt your house and the fix never happened, a lender may refuse to fund the buyer's loan until it is done. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands avoids that problem, but you should still tell the buyer what you know.

Wet winters strain crawl spaces, gutters and old siding too, and inspectors check for moisture first.

The deed tax formula is found in Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The deed should be accompanied by proof of the actual purchase price on a Department of Revenue form. Only value above a mortgage that already paid its own mortgage tax is counted, and a recording fee is charged on top.

A sale that closes late in the year may overlap the tax bill. Call the Tuscaloosa County tax office before closing day to learn the current balance and any unpaid earlier years, and to confirm how the office handles payoffs.

  • Request the current tax figure early.
  • Collect payoff amounts for any mortgage, judgment or code fine.
  • Sign the deed before a notary, following the closing agent's directions.

Cash suits owners for whom speed or condition outweighs the last few thousand dollars a repaired listing might yield. In Tuscaloosa you often see:

  • A student rental in need of paint, new flooring and cleaning after a lease ends.
  • An inherited home that relatives dispute or do not want to keep up.
  • A property whose storm or roof damage would worry an appraiser.
  • An owner who has to move for a job.

The path runs like this. Tell us about the house and we make an offer. After you accept, a title company or attorney verifies ownership, requests payoffs and schedules the closing. You sign the deed, the loan and taxes are cleared from the proceeds, and the balance goes to you. Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate paperwork and any lease.

We buy houses in Tuscaloosa as they are, and the decision to accept is yours. Asking costs nothing, and you can hold our figure up against a listing agent's.

sections.h2: If you owe on the house
sections.html:
A mortgage balance, a back tax bill or a lien does not stand in the way of selling. The title company asks your lender for a payoff letter and the county for the current tax figure, and both are paid from the sale proceeds before you receive anything. Code fines and unpaid utility bills turn up in the title search and are handled the same way.

Ask to see the title search early. If something is attached to the property that you did not expect, you can decide whether to clear it or to adjust your price, instead of learning about it at the table. Add up the payoffs against the offer so you know what you will take home.

If you are behind on payments, tell the buyer at the start. A firm closing date can matter more than a higher number when a lender is waiting.

Begin by finding out who has authority to sign. Visit the probate office or an attorney, and collect the deed and estate papers. Relatives who disagree about selling often get stuck here, so settle that point before you invite offers. When the paperwork is clear, a closing can move fast because a cash purchase needs no lender approval.

Plan a few weeks ahead for the practical pieces. Ask the county for the tax balance, ask your lender for a payoff letter and confirm that every name on the deed will be able to sign. If one owner lives elsewhere, ask the title company whether the documents can be notarized by mail.

On closing day, read the settlement statement before you sign. It should show the sale price, each payoff, the recording costs and your net. If a number looks wrong, ask the closer to explain it first. Take photos of the empty house, hand over the keys and cancel or transfer the utilities.

If tenants are still in the house, agree in writing on who handles the security deposit and the last month's rent. That one conversation heads off most disputes after closing.

faqs.a: Tuscaloosa County, and the city is its seat. It lies on the Black Warrior River.
Yes, from 1826 to 1846. The capital then moved to Montgomery.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Tuscaloosa?
faqs.a: October 1 is the due date and December 31 is the last day before delinquency. The county tax office can quote your balance.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on a Tuscaloosa sale?
faqs.a: The state sets it at 50 cents per $500 of value. The probate judge collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tuscaloosa house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can take it in its current condition, and we buy as is.
